title: Normalized polynomial models compute intrinsic relative-duality base change
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated, flat, locally finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with $S$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $(D_f,\xi_f)$ be its coherent relative dualizing pair [def-trf-coherent-relative-dualizing-pair] with the normalized polynomial-chart comparisons of [lem-trf-relative-duality-polynomial-chart]. For a morphism $a:S'\to S$ with $S'$ locally Noetherian, put $X'=X\times_SS'$, $b:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. There is a unique isomorphism in the derived category of module sheaves [def-pc-derived-category]
$$\beta_a:Lb^*D_f\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{f'}$$
sending the derived pullback of $\xi_f$ to $\xi_{f'}$; derived pullback uses [def-pc-derived-pullback]. These isomorphisms respect identities and composition and are natural under isomorphisms of $S$-families. On affine charts $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ over $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and a polynomial presentation $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$, for every affine $\operatorname{Spec}R'\subset S'$ mapping to $V$, set $P'=P\otimes_RR'$ and $B'=B\otimes_RR'$. Under the specified polynomial-chart comparisons, $\beta_a$ is the derived-Hom comparison
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_P(B,\Omega^n_{P/R})[n]\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_{P'}(B',\Omega^n_{P'/R'})[n].$$
Differentials and their top exterior powers use [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra], and derived Hom uses [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] with its natural $B$-action. If $F^\bullet\to B[0]$ is a bounded finite projective $P$-resolution, the map is represented, after forgetting to $P'$, by extension of scalars of $\operatorname{Hom}_P(F^\bullet,\Omega^n_{P/R})$: a pure tensor $h\otimes r'$ acts by $z\otimes s'\mapsto r's'(h(z)\otimes1)$. It commutes with open restriction and the normalized ordered polynomial-refinement comparisons, including the contraction of the extra equation $t-u$ with $\mathrm d(t-u)$ to $1$. If $f$ is also proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], these pair comparisons agree with those of $f^!\mathcal O_S$, where $f^!$ is the right adjoint of derived quasi-coherent direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image], under the intrinsic proper-duality identification of [lem-sfb-proper-flat-dualizing-polynomial-model]. In particular, if $f$ is proper and $f^!\mathcal O_S\simeq\omega_f[d]$, $f'^!\mathcal O_{S'}\simeq\omega_{f'}[d]$ for finite locally free modules $\omega_f=H^{-d}(f^!\mathcal O_S)$ and $\omega_{f'}=H^{-d}(f'^!\mathcal O_{S'})$, then the base-change isomorphism $b^*\omega_f\simeq\omega_{f'}$ of relative dualizing modules, namely $H^{-d}$ of the base-change isomorphism $Lb^*f^!\mathcal O_S\simeq f'^!\mathcal O_{S'}$, is $H^{-d}(\beta_a)$, using $H^{-d}(Lb^*(\omega_f[d]))=b^*\omega_f$ for locally free $\omega_f$. No local complete-intersection, nodal, dimension or Gorenstein hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Fix $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$ above $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ and $V'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\subset S'$ mapping to $V$. The affine pair comparison gives precisely flatness, finite presentation and Noetherianity of $R\to B$. The polynomial-quotient perfection theorem supplies a bounded finite projective $P$-resolution $F\to B[0]$, for every chosen polynomial presentation $P\twoheadrightarrow B$. Write $L=\Omega^n_{P/R}$ and $C=C_B^P(L)[n]$. The specified chart comparison identifies $D_f|_U$ with $C$ as a normalized pair, not merely with its underlying complex.

Here $B'=B\otimes_RR'$ and $P'=P\otimes_RR'$. The pair $(B,P')$ is Tor independent over $P$: if $G\to R'[0]$ is a free $R$-resolution, then $P\otimes_RG$ is a free $P$-resolution of $P'$, and $B\otimes_RG\to B'$ is exact since $B$ is $R$-flat. Hence the exchange lemma applies to $(P,B,P')$ and $L$, without requiring $R\to R'$ flat. Its coefficient is $L\otimes_PP'\cong\Omega^n_{P'/R'}$: polynomial derivations have basis $dx_i$, and the isomorphism sends each ordered wedge to the same ordered wedge after extending coefficients. We obtain an isomorphism $c:C\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\to C'$ in $D(B')$, with the required $B'$-action. The affine derived-pullback comparison identifies its source with $(Lb^*D_f)|_{U\times_VV'}$.

proof.text: The same exchange statement gives the claimed representative after forgetting to $P'$: $(h\otimes r')(z\otimes s')=r's'(h(z)\otimes1)$. Indeed its counit at the unit is evaluation of $h$ extended by $R'$, so this is the prescribed derived-Hom map, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of its source and target. The bounded finite projective Hom complex and its extension compute the two underlying derived objects by that statement. Shifting both sides by $n$ keeps the formula unchanged. Thus the representative applies to every such $F$, independently of its choice.

source.place: Tag 0BZP, equation-base-change, with the finite-projective Hom representative.

proof.text: Let $Q=B\otimes_RB$ and $Q'=B'\otimes_{R'}B'$. The derived pullback of the diagonal object is $B\otimes_Q^{\mathbf L}Q'\simeq B'$: resolve $R'$ freely over $R$, extend to $Q$ (which is $R$-flat), then tensor with the $R$-flat $B$. Derived-pullback composition identifies the pulled-back target of the diagonal class with $Lp_1'^*(Lb^*D_f)$. On the affine charts the class is therefore the $v'$ of the scalar-naturality lemma. Apply that lemma with $T=C$. Both $C$ and $C'$ have the required pseudo-coherence and relative Tor bounds by the polynomial-chart theorem. Since $\rho_C(\xi_C)=1_C$, the lemma gives $\rho'_{C\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'}(\xi_C')=c^{-1}$. Naturality in the target now gives $\rho'_{C'}((c\otimes_{B',p_1'}Q')\xi_C')=1_{C'}=\rho'_{C'}(\xi_{C'})$. The bijection implies equality of these classes. Thus the explicit $c$ is class preserving, including its normalization by $1$, not only preservation of the rank-one span.

source.place: Tags 0E2E and 0E2F; scalar-naturality refinement of the diagonal adjunction.

proof.text: The formula of Step 3 commutes with localization: both paths send $(h\otimes r')$ evaluated on $z\otimes s'$ to the localized value of $r's'h(z)$. The tensor and Hom open-restriction comparisons identify this calculation with restriction of the sheaf objects. For a one-coordinate refinement use the two-term graph resolution with differential $t-u$. Its extension has differential $t-u'$ and the dual evaluation sends $(t-u)^\vee\otimes d(t-u)$ to $1$, hence after extension sends $(t-u')^\vee\otimes d(t-u')$ to $1$. For several coordinates the tensor formula retains their order and degrees, so every sign $(-1)^{ij}$ agrees before and after extension. The polynomial-chart theorem supplies the normalized refinement maps and their cocycles; the displayed calculation verifies commutation with each generating refinement. Two presentations compare through their combined-variable presentation, so the comparison commutes with all the specified ordered refinements.

proof.text: Put $K=Lb^*D_f$ and $L=D_{f'}$. Steps 2 and 4 identify $(K,\xi')$ locally with the normalized polynomial pair for $f'$. Consequently $K$ is pseudo-coherent, has locally finite relative Tor amplitude, and multiplication by $\xi'$ is an isomorphism: each of these conditions is checked on the displayed local models, with derived Hom restricted by the open-restriction comparison. The base-changed affine charts form a cover; taking affine refinements gives a basis, and no intersection is assumed affine. Thus $(K,\xi')$ and $(L,\xi_{f'})$ are both supplied relative dualizing pairs. Rigidity gives their unique class-preserving isomorphism $\beta_a$. On every such chart rigidity again applies, so its restriction is exactly $c$. This obtains the global map and the polynomial formula simultaneously; no descent of arbitrary derived morphisms from their local values is assumed.

For the identity base map, the identity of the pair preserves its class and hence equals $\beta_{1}$. For $S''\xrightarrow{a'}S'\xrightarrow{a}S$, the composite $\beta_{a'}\circ Lb'^*(\beta_a)$ sends the twice-pulled diagonal class to $\xi_{f''}$. Under the unital associative pullback comparisons, twice-pulled and directly pulled classes agree. The composite therefore equals $\beta_{aa'}$ by rigidity. An isomorphism of $S$-families takes the diagonal, its multiplication and the projections to their counterparts; pullback transports the defining pair condition. The two comparisons in the resulting naturality square are class-preserving isomorphisms between the same supplied pairs, so rigidity makes them equal. These arguments include empty schemes and do not require globally finite covers.

source.place: duality.tex Tags 0E2W and 0E4P; uniqueness proves identity, composition and isomorphism naturality.

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is proper. The intrinsic proper-duality polynomial-model theorem identifies $f^!\mathcal O_S$ and $f'^!\mathcal O_{S'}$ with their relative dualizing pairs and with the same normalized chart models. Transport $\beta_a$ along these pair identifications. It is the unique class-preserving isomorphism from $Lb^*f^!\mathcal O_S$ to $f'^!\mathcal O_{S'}$. This is precisely the intrinsic pair comparison of proper duality; uniqueness rules out an additional unit or sign. On charts it is the same $c$ already computed, so all the restriction and refinement compatibilities persist.

source.place: duality.tex Tags 0E2Z and 0E4P, with the supplied intrinsic proper-duality identification.

proof.text: Finally assume the stated concentration and finite local freeness. On an open where $\omega_f\cong\mathcal O_X^r$, its degree-zero complex is a flat model, so $Lb^*(\omega_f[d])\cong(b^*\omega_f)[d]$. Taking $H^{-d}$ gives $b^*\omega_f$; the same calculation identifies $H^{-d}(f'^!\mathcal O_{S'})$ with $\omega_{f'}$. Cohomology is a functor, so the equality of derived comparisons in Step 8 gives equality of the induced module comparisons. These identifications are independent of the trivialization because ordinary pullback and cohomology act on transition matrices by the same entrywise ring map. Hence the module base-change map is exactly $H^{-d}(\beta_a)$ under the stated identifications.

source.place: Degree-zero flat model and functoriality of cohomology; consequence of Step 8.
